content:
alex: heads up — after the kernel routing change in canary we started seeing ~2x OOMs on the 8xA100 nightly. dumping trace + small perf profile, posting repro and knobs I used below.

maria: can you paste the allocator knobs you had set for the canary?

alex: config snapshot: ```
expandable_segments=true
max_split_size_mb=32
garbage_collection_threshold=0.25
workspace_mb=4096
```
also note: kernel routing switched to v2 tiling by default in that build.

devon: interesting — traces show a lot of tiny frees / alloc churn. kernel v2 moves more ops into narrower kernels which increases fragmentation risk. could be slab split/fragmentation. what are kv-cache hit patterns during the warmup?

alex: kv-cache saw a warmup spike and more misses; quick log line: `kvcache.misses +420%` during the first 2k requests. prefix growth + large transient allocations.

sasha: quick triage idea :thinking:  lower expandable_segments (stop aggressive micro-splits), increase max_split_size_mb (fewer splits), and make GC more aggressive so it reclaims earlier. try: 
```
# quick canary command
reroute-canary --set expandable_segments=false \n               --set max_split_size_mb=128 \n               --set garbage_collection_threshold=0.5
```
This reduces split churn at the cost of slightly larger slabs.

maria: won't that increase internal waste for long-running jobs?

devon: it might, but our profile shows fragmentation by many tiny freed segments that are not being coalesced. fewer splits -> fewer non-reclaimable heads. also enable workspace buffer reuse to amortize temp allocs: `workspace.reuse=true`.

alex: ran a dev canary with those 3 tweaks for 30min. results: no OOMs, p50 +5ms, throughput -3% tokens/sec. GC cycles increased (ran earlier): ~120 GC events/s vs ~45/s previously. quick flame summary pasted: ```
flame: alloc:50%, kernel:35%, cuda:15%
```

sasha: nice. can we add split/merge counters to confirm the hypothesis? if merges are low and splits high that points to coalesce problem. also check per-slab free-list lengths.

infra-bot: canary deploy status: cluster=test-7 build=r2026 — deploy ok, health checks passed.

maria: if the knob changes stabilize memory we should document recommendations and start an A/B rollout (10% -> 50%). include canary durations and perf guardrails.

devon: also add a synthetic perf test that reproduces kv-warmup burst and kernel v2 tiling to catch regressions in CI. this should be part of the allocator integration tests.

alex: will open a small playbook + repro harness. leaving the mini repro command here: ```
python repro.py --model bert --tokens 512 --warmup 1000 --knobs expandable_segments=false,max_split_size_mb=128,gc_threshold=0.5
```
@sasha can you follow up with counters and a tiny perf job?

sasha: yep — I'll add split/merge counters, free-list histograms, and a 15m perf job that runs the kv-warmup scenario tomorrow. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks folks — saved the logs and pprof in the gist (link pasted in thread). will prod this into a controlled canary next.
